entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: This is the first application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, as he / she is implicated in connection with Crime No.471/2022 registered at Police Station Rawti, District Ratlam (MP) for offence punishable under Section Section 376, 352 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860t.
The applicant is in custody since 21/01/2023.
Allegation against the applicant is of rape.
Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated by the prosecutrix who is 29 years old.

It is submitted that the date of incident is said to be 04/12/2022 whereas the FIR has been lodged on 10/12/2022 i.e. after a period of 6 days, thus, admittedly there is no FSL report or medical report on record favourable to the prosecution bu the same also fortifies the applicant's objection that he has been falsely implicated in the case.

It is further submitted that Ganesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28553210/
1 the charge sheet has already been filed, applicant is in jail since 21/01/2023 and the final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

entities.text: Ganesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and he be released on bail.

Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the incident took place on 04/12/2022, thereafter it was referred to the Bheel Panchayat and subsequently the FIR has been lodged, thus, it is submitted that the delay has been properly explained in the case, hence, no case for grant of bail is made out.

Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case diary and also considering the fact that the only incriminating material against the applicant is the statement of the prosecutrix recorded after more than 6 days of the incident and there is no other material available on record to connect him with the offence and the fact that the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, in the considered opinion of this Court, the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE krjoshi Ganesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28553210/
